paragraphs: R' Yitzchak bar Abba bar Machsya.

He was a disciple of Rav. In Megillah, chapter 2, he sat with Rav Chananel before Rav: one said יהודים and the other יהודיים. In [Berakhot, chapter 6, halakhah 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.6.6), Yitzchak bar Abba bar Machsya and Rav Chananel are mentioned: one said, “Blessed is He she-natan,” meaning “who gave.” They went up to Rav’s house and heard bar Chona (read: Rav Huna), in Rav’s name, say “asher natan,” also meaning “who gave,” etc.[^1][^2]

notes.text: ח״א means “one said,” supported by the spelled-out חד אמר below; it does not denote two textual versions. The two Hebrew forms יהודים and יהודיים and the contrasted blessing forms שנתן and אשר נתן remain distinct. סלקון is “they went up,” not “we went up.” ושמעון is read contextually as the Aramaic “and they heard,” rather than as the personal name Shimon; this makes the visit and reported blessing coherent. The supplied בר חונה and Hyman’s parenthetic צ״ל רב הונא are both retained. The full Megillah locator פ״ב סה״ב is left unconverted; no modern halakhah is guessed. Neither passage nor the parenthetic correction was independently checked in the earlier preparation; the subsequent limited Berakhot title comparison is noted below.

The abbreviated heading title is retained as R'. The Guggenheimer edition of Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:6:6 names Yitzchak bar Abba bar Machsya without a title, while explicitly retaining the full forms for Chananel and Rav and a bracketed full form before Chuna. Hyman’s explicit full titles, including his parenthetic Rav Huna, are preserved without using them to infer Yitzchak’s title.
